focus: P6 recovery semantics across compile, claim/fence, budget, human gate, nogood, belief, and stale-premise failures
noveltyJustification: Iteration 010 defined the refusal envelope and generic recovery classes; this pass resolves P6 with boundary-specific stable actions, retry predicates, non-mutation assertions, audit-versus-telemetry persistence, and concrete Graphene mismatch findings.
keyFindings: Stable advisory action enums are separate from code-owned retry prerequisites and never carry authority
Compile failures retry only after changed proposal or named compiler/policy inputs and mint no gateway decision
Claim/head/fence recovery requires fresh claimant-addressed proof, request identity, and full reauthorization
Budget recovery preserves debit history and requires a new compile or governed allocation change
Human waiting, context refresh, timeout, and decision refusal are distinct transitions with distinct mutation rules
Belief and nogood recovery is predicate-specific and dirty-base quarantine is not candidate refusal
Refusal response, gateway denial audit, and operational telemetry are separate persistence boundaries

ruledOut.approach: Use one retryable boolean or surface-local suggestion as recovery protocol
ruledOut.reason: Failure families require different fresh proofs and authority

ruledOut.approach: Reuse observed head fence claim or gate context from a refusal
ruledOut.reason: Boundary observations may be stale at delivery and carry no capability
Committed debits and root allocation survive restart

ruledOut.approach: Treat human wait or timeout as generic retry
ruledOut.reason: Waiting preserves the gate and timeout is a separate authorized event

ruledOut.approach: Repair a dirty nogood during candidate admission
ruledOut.reason: Candidate refusal and dirty-base quarantine have different causation and authority

ruledOut.approach: Require no append anywhere on refusal
ruledOut.reason: Domain state remains unchanged while gateway denial requires one non-domain audit decision

nextFocus: P7 human gates over live belief context and invalidation semantics
